TL:DR - You WILL get banned for using macros (7 days) and the game is VERY PAY TO WIN. The only reason this game has good reviews is because of "OG" players. They're huffing Copium and nostalgia that's stopping them from seeing how awful the games state is. This review won't be short but won't be terribly long either. So, let's discuss: I've played this game with my brother since me and him were kids. We loved it. However, we spent a LOT of money on just the simplest guns in game. How much is a lot? For one gun? About $72-$200. Now I normally wouldn't be mad about these outlandish prices for PIXEL GUNS, IF there was an easy way to earn Graalets.(In-game currency) The only way to actually earn Graalets is by working at a pizza shop which pays 10-20 for 1 pizza made, digging for shells which is very hit or miss and daily quests which is randomized everyday but CAN reward 1k Graalets depending on the challenge. Keep in mind you're going to be grinding your butt off just for some pixel melee or gun that consumes 90% of your currency. Aside from the pay to win aspect which ruins the game for anyone with a brain, the admins are children LITERALLY and metaphorically. Some admins are also very corrupt and biased for some people. I've seen admins give specific people free items that are normally very expensive. The game in of itself is just very old and outdated. Theres a LOT of content but most of it requires thousands of hours of gameplay, requires you to try VERY HARD, don't forget that macros are a 7 day bannable offense. Before i go, heres some math. The BAR (best gun in the game) costs 200k Graalets. You can purchase 27k Graalets for 9.99. This adds up to $72 worth of graalets required to purchase ONE INGAME PIXEL (Non resellable) GUN. Now, if we macro, we will obtain approximately 1500 Graalets an hour. With that being said, it would require a CONSTANT 133 HOURS (of constant pizza farming) JUST TO OBTAIN THE BAR. Disgusting. Get this trash off of steam. Until they allow macros, I'm going to keep this review negative.

GraalOnline Era, developed by GraalOnline and published by Toonslab, is a free-to-play massively multiplayer online action RPG that brings a modern urban twist to the classic top-down multiplayer formula. Originally part of the long-running Graal Online ecosystem, the game eventually made its way to Steam in 2024, introducing a broader PC audience to a world that had previously thrived primarily on mobile platforms. Unlike many MMORPGs that rely on structured quests, elaborate narratives, or large fantasy worlds, GraalOnline Era emphasizes social interaction, player competition, and sandbox freedom within a persistent multiplayer city. The result is an experience that feels more like a living online community than a traditional role-playing campaign, where the activities and conflicts of players shape much of the game’s moment-to-moment excitement. The setting of Era stands out immediately because it abandons the typical medieval fantasy themes associated with many MMORPGs and instead places players in a gritty, stylized urban environment dominated by gangs, weapon shops, and bustling city districts. Players begin by creating a customizable character who enters this open city world and gradually becomes involved in its underground conflicts. Firearms, melee weapons, and street combat replace swords and magic, giving the game a distinctly modern tone. Rival gangs battle over territory, players patrol city streets looking for fights or alliances, and the entire world operates as a constantly evolving multiplayer sandbox where hundreds of players can interact simultaneously. One of the most defining gameplay systems in GraalOnline Era is its gang system, which allows players to join or create organized groups that compete for dominance across various bases in the city. These gang bases act as strategic control points that can be captured and defended, often leading to intense battles between teams of players. During peak activity, these conflicts can escalate into chaotic group fights involving dozens of participants, with bullets flying across the screen and players scrambling to defend their positions. Because the game’s combat takes place in real time within the shared world, these battles feel spontaneous and unpredictable, making gang warfare one of the central attractions for competitive players. The combat mechanics themselves are relatively simple but fast and responsive. Viewed from a top-down perspective, players can move around the environment while firing weapons such as pistols, rifles, and shotguns. Each weapon type has different firing patterns and ranges, encouraging players to experiment with different loadouts depending on their preferred playstyle. Some players favor rapid-fire weapons that allow aggressive attacks, while others rely on stronger firearms that reward careful positioning. Melee weapons also exist for close-range encounters, adding another layer of strategy when battles become crowded. While the system may not offer the complexity of modern shooter games, its accessibility makes it easy for newcomers to jump into fights while still rewarding experienced players who master movement and positioning. Beyond combat, GraalOnline Era places a strong emphasis on personalization and player expression. One of the game’s most beloved features is its customization system, which allows players to modify their characters with a wide range of outfits, hats, accessories, and other cosmetic items. The game even allows players to upload their own pixel art designs for clothing, leading to a vibrant community culture where players create and share unique fashion styles. Walking through the city often reveals hundreds of distinctive character appearances, giving the world a lively and creative atmosphere shaped by the community itself. Housing and decoration systems further expand this personalization aspect. Players can purchase homes and furnish them with furniture, decorations, and various collectibles obtained throughout the game. These homes often become gathering spots where friends meet, trade items, or simply socialize away from the chaos of gang warfare. Some players treat housing as a creative outlet, carefully designing elaborate interior layouts that reflect their personality. This system adds a surprising social dimension to the game, transforming it into more than just a combat-focused experience. For players who prefer alternative activities, the game also includes a variety of jobs and side tasks that allow them to earn currency without constantly fighting other players. These jobs can range from simple labor activities to small quests and special event tasks that reward participation with money or unique items. Seasonal events are also periodically introduced, bringing themed content, temporary shops, and exclusive collectibles that encourage players to revisit the game during holidays or special occasions. While these systems are relatively simple compared to larger MMORPGs, they help create a sense of variety and give players different ways to interact with the world. Visually, GraalOnline Era maintains the retro 2D style that has defined the Graal series for many years. Characters are represented through pixel-style sprites, and the environments use simple but colorful tile-based designs. While the graphics are clearly dated compared to modern MMORPGs, the simplicity serves a functional purpose by keeping the action readable during large multiplayer fights. The art style also contributes to the nostalgic charm of the game, reminiscent of classic online RPGs from the early days of internet gaming. The social aspect of the game is arguably its most important feature. Unlike many modern online games that separate players through instanced content or matchmaking systems, GraalOnline Era thrives on shared public spaces where everyone interacts within the same persistent world. Players trade items, chat in crowded areas, form friendships, organize gangs, and even host informal events. Over time, this social interaction creates a sense of community that gives the game its lasting appeal. Many players return not only for the gameplay but also for the relationships and rivalries that develop within the city. However, the game does have some noticeable drawbacks. Its graphics and mechanics may feel outdated to players accustomed to modern MMORPG standards, and the simple combat system can become repetitive over long sessions. The open PvP environment can also be intimidating for newcomers, as experienced players often dominate certain areas. Additionally, while the sandbox structure offers freedom, the lack of a strong narrative or guided progression may leave some players unsure of what to do when they first enter the world. Despite these limitations, GraalOnline Era succeeds in offering a distinctive multiplayer experience built around community interaction and competitive gang warfare. Its open city, flexible customization systems, and lively player base create a world that feels active and unpredictable. While it may not appeal to players looking for deep storylines or cutting-edge visuals, it remains an engaging social sandbox where creativity, rivalry, and player-driven activities shape the experience. For those who enjoy persistent online worlds and competitive multiplayer environments, GraalOnline Era provides a surprisingly lively and enduring digital playground. Rating: 7/10

This game is basically a virtual playground for whales. Everything is overly expensive, and all the new stuff that comes out is increasingly more expensive than before. I thought the bar was overpriced as hell 10 years ago, but now we've got guns double the price of that. The grind is so bad that you're better off working a real job and just buying in-game currency. 10 bucks for roughly 30k, while you literally need to shovel sand in the game for like 15-20 hours to get the same amount. You could argue this is part of the gameplay loop, but no, they're using this as a cope to excuse the lack of actual in-game content and activities. The only redeeming factor is the events, where you have a chance to earn something decent if you're willing to put the hours in. To actually play and enjoy the game, you have to dump roughly 100 euros into in-game currency just to afford a decent gun, since 90% of the cheap/budget guns are filler junk that'll basically scam you. And then... congratulations, you just saved yourself approximately a THOUSAND HOURS of mind-numbing grind and unlocked "FUN." You can now carelessly mow down all the peasants struggling to make money by collecting trash on the streets. That is, if you can find any of them. Not many are left to shoot. The game hovers around average 900 players, but a solid 80% of them are grinding for money in safe zones. You've got maybe 40 people in Plasma and a handful roaming the streets. The rest are holding gang territory or just AFK somewhere. Whales are the only reason Graal still functions to this day. The whole operation is allegedly being run by a skeleton crew with a nonexistent owner and has been for the past 10 years. Literally nothing has changed, they're still understaffed, and the people managing the game are incompetent beyond belief. It's a mystery how this company manages to function, but I guess the endless amount of money handed to them by whales willing to buy and spend 2 mil worth of currency (roughly 700 euros, btw) on some flashy sword from auction is enough to keep the lights on. They run auctions like this constantly, for multiple items at a time, probably enough to cover payroll for every employee they have and somehow, someway, things are still horrible and unchanged. Support is obviously nonexistent as well given all that, and you'll wait weeks just for a reply. The general infrastructure around the company and the game is so lacklustre and questionable it makes you wonder if this is all just a big money laundering operation. If you want to cope and relive your childhood for like 2 weeks, the game isn't all that bad. But after that, you'll start wondering if your past self was... "slow" for enduring this. In reality, this game isn't free, because the only way to enjoy it long-term is to get rid of the endless grind by swiping your card. Only then can you actually take part in the gang-related activities and other PVP aspects and PVP is the ONLY thing left to do. The social part of the game is completely gone. Clubs, churches, other hangout spots are all entirely empty. No one talks to you unless they want to trade or do business, and even then, most players have chat turned off, or aren't fluent in English when they do talk. All of this is only a fraction of the issues this game has and I'm sure other reviews cover things I have left out. I've mostly refrained from using strong language, but believe me, no one is happy about the state of the game and the people behind it. If you do not mind that you are directly enriching actual greedlord jew ♥♥♥♥♥♥ who does not care about you in the slightest, I guess you can give it a go. I'd still advise you to not spend any money on this game, it's not worth it at all, but if you insist, only buy enough for a weapon and never again.
